newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PREMIER TO DESIGNATE NEW FARM MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PREMIER TO DESIGNATE NEW FARM MINISTER.

text.p: A little-known member of Poland's co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL), Jaroslaw Kalinowski, looked set on Tuesday to become the new agriculture minister this week.
Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said the prime minister would ask the president to appoint Kalinowski as the minister and one of three deputy prime ministers.

The powerful agriculture ministry and its associated vice-premiership is controlled by the Peasants under their coalition agreement with their larger partner in government, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD).

If President Aleksander Kwasniewski nominates Kalinowski, 35, he will take over the posts vacated earlier in April by the liberal Roman Jagielinski, who was sacked after losing the support of most of his own PSL party.

"Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz will send to the president a motion to nominate Kalinowski as the new agriculture minister," Jakubowska told Reuters on Tuesday. "It is a matter of a day or two."

The SLD's Cimoszewicz, who disagreed with the Peasants over their criticism of the former farm minister, has been long reluctant to appoint Kalinowski fearing he might try to radically change the government's agriculture policies.
But Jakubowska said that the prime minister's doubts had been dispelled during his meeting with Kalinowski on Tuesday.
"It turned out that the prime minister's and Mr Kalinowski's views on various issues had more in common than earlier expected," she said.
Cimoszewicz was forced to dismiss Jagielinski, leader of the more market-oriented faction in the Peasant Party, after the majority of the group's leadership attacked his policies.

The majority -- led by Peasant party president Waldemar Pawlak and representing small farm owners keen to uphold state protection of agriculture -- accused him of policies resulting in a food trade deficit last year and low grain prices for domestic farmers.

Many analysts dismissed these allegations as unfounded and suggested the attack on Jagielinski was designed to distance the party from the government's record, in the eyes of its own farming electorate, before elections due around September.
Kalinowski's candidacy for the agriculture portfolio was put forward by Pawlak, whom Jagielinski unsuccessfully challenged for the party's leadership last year.

Kalinowski's nomination will resolve the latest in a long series of conflicts within the nearly four-year-old government coalition, which is expected to last until the parliamentary elections. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
